[build-system].requires: which is a list of dependencies needed to build the project – this is typically just the build backend package, but it may also contain additional dependencies. You can also constrain the versions, e.g., requires = ['setuptools >= 61.0'].
[project].dependencies: If your project has dependencies, list them.A dependency specification always specifies a distribution name.This is an example:[project] dependencies = ['https']
[project.optional-dependencies]: You may want to make some of your dependencies optional, if they are only needed for a specific feature of your package. In that case, put them in optional-dependencies like [project.optional-dependencies] gui = ['PyQt5']
[build-system].build-backend: The [build-system] table contains a build-backend key, which specifies the build backend to be used.
[project.scripts]: To install a command as part of your package, declare it in the [project.scripts] table like [project.scripts] spam-cli = 'spam:main_cli'
[project.entry-points.'yourplugin.plugin: To create such a plugin, you need to declare it in a subtable of [project.entry-points] like this: [project.entry-points.'spam.magical'] tomatoes = 'spam:main_tomatoes'
[tool.setuptools].script-files: equivalent to the script keyword in setup.py. Whenever possible, please use project.scripts instead.
